audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 3, 5 and 6 disagree with the already-audited mirror (ksante__warwick), which set the chart to Skill / K'Sante / K'Sante / K'Sante / Skill / Skill / Warwick.
audit.why: The two directions must agree. The mirror's shape is also the kit-supported one: All Out explicitly trades defenses for damage, which is exactly what a two-item %max-health bite punishes.
audit.corrected: Rows 3, 5 and 6 flipped on both layers as one atomic group, with whys[6] rewritten so the prose stops saying the opposite of its own row.
sources: enemyKit R text ('at the cost of reduced defenses')

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text ends 'before he stacks Pentakill' — Pentakill is not an ability, an item or a mechanic in this matchup.
audit.why: K'Sante's stacking mechanic is Ntofo Strikes: each hit grants a stack, and at 2 stacks he fires a shockwave that PULLS enemies in. Nothing called Pentakill exists here.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the real Ntofo Strikes stack behaviour and the fact that the pull is gone once the second stack is spent.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three separate errors. phases[4].why and breakdown.late call Infinite Duress a 'point-and-click fight starter'. spikes[1].text claims your R 'channels through his base Ntofo pull attempts'. spikes[3].text claims 'his empowered W stuns you mid-R'.
audit.why: Infinite Duress is a directional leap suppressing the first champion collided with for 1.5s, 110s at rank 1, and the kit flags it as an interruptible channel — it does not power through anything. And Riot's Path Maker text is explicit: when All Out, it deals increased damage and NO LONGER knocks back or stuns. The page states the exact opposite of the ability text.
audit.corrected: R restated as a missable 1.5s leap-suppress on a 110s cooldown; the sequencing is bait Path Maker's damage-reduction charge (14s at rank 1) then commit; and All Out's loss of the W stun plus its reduced defenses is now stated as your late-game window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flagged 'Your Eternal Hunger' in whys[0] as a probable wrong ability name.
audit.why: False positive — Eternal Hunger is Warwick's passive, the below-50%/below-25% healing on his attacks. It is correctly used.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click fight starter that locks his carry tool. Reassess every all-in at 6 — K'Sante's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Infinite Duress leaps onto the first champion it hits for 1.5s, 110s at rank 1. He baits it with Path Maker's damage-reduction charge — spend it after.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click fight starter that locks his carry tool — build your teamfight around that. K'Sante carry threat: 7/10 — anti-heal stays core, shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Infinite Duress leaps onto the first champion in its path for 1.5s — line it up, it can miss. K'Sante carry threat: 7/10 — anti-heal stays core, shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.

edits.before: With all three abilities you out-sustain K'Sante's Ntofo Strikes poke: Q healing plus Eternal Hunger passive lets you shrug his early trades, and once his Q charges are spent you can W-empowered burst him before he stacks Pentakill.
edits.after: With all three abilities you out-sustain K'Sante's Ntofo Strikes poke: Q healing plus Eternal Hunger lets you shrug his trades, and once his second Ntofo stack is spent the shockwave pull is gone — burst him with Blood Hunt speed then.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a hard answer to K'Sante's non-ult form: he can't All Out yet, so your R suppression channels through his base Ntofo pull attempts and you win any level-6 skirmish outright.
edits.after: Infinite Duress leaps onto the first champion it hits for a 1.5s suppress and is 110s at rank 1, so he will bait it behind Path Maker's damage reduction (14s) — spend it after that charge, not into it.

edits.before: Late K'Sante with two+ items becomes a walking peel: All Out repositions you into his team and his empowered W stuns you mid-R, so pick him off the map instead of dueling.
edits.after: Late K'Sante repositions you with All Out, but in that form Path Maker no longer knocks back or stuns and his defenses drop — that is when your %max-health bite kills him.

edits.before: At 6 your Infinite Duress suppresses his pre-All-Out form for a guaranteed kill.
edits.after: At 6 Infinite Duress is a 1.5s leap-suppress; he baits it with Path Maker.

edits.before: Past two items his percent-health true damage and peel outscale your sustain entirely.
edits.after: Past two items, All Out's dropped defenses let your %max-health bite kill him.

notes: The two directions of this matchup still disagree about who owns 2+ items in prose: I flipped the row to Warwick per the mirror and grounded it on All Out's stated 'reduced defenses', but `late` still reads 'every duel favours him past two items'. I did not rewrite `late` because I would be asserting a scaling claim I cannot verify beyond that one kit line — flagging it instead. Also unresolved: the kit puts the trueDamage flag on Path Maker (W), while the page attributes percent-health true damage to his empowered strikes; I left spikes[2].text alone rather than guess which is right.
